events.title: Make Believe: Magic, the Worlds of the Jim Henson Company
events.location: GOMA, Stanley Place, South Bank
events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: Celebrating 70 years of creativity and innovation, the exclusive-to-Brisbane exhibition ‘Make, Believe, Magic: The Worlds of The Jim Henson Company’ will be an unprecedented exploration of world-building and imaginative storytelling. Founded by Jim and Jane Henson in 1955, The Jim Henson Company has created some of the most cherished characters in screen history and continues to revolutionise the art of puppetry for television and film. Their indelible imprint on entertainment, education and popular culture globally is seen in the much-loved series Fraggle Rock and Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock, the treasured fantasy worlds of The Dark Crystal and Labyrinth, the iconic characters of the Muppets, and the instantly recognisable residents of Sesame Street. In a world-first, ‘Make, Believe, Magic: The Worlds of The Jim Henson Company’ will include the Great Hall set from the Emmy Award-winning television series Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock, taking audiences behind the scenes of a working puppeteer’s film set. Immense and immersive, the exhibition will explore the Company’s dynamic trajectory from practical puppetry to today’s animatronic and digital innovations, as well as its ongoing dedication to the craft of creature design and trailblazing developments in on-screen puppeteering. It will feature hundreds of objects, from practical puppets and animatronic creatures to props, costumes, original drawings and moving image clips. Screening alongside the exhibition throughout its run will be three, free film programs at GOMA’s Australian Cinémathèque as well as a suite of QAGOMA’s renowned public, learning and access programs inviting audiences to explore and engage with the exhibition themes and artworks. This exhibition is organised by the Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art in collaboration with The Jim Henson Company. QAGOMA is excited to be celebrating the opening of ‘Make, Believe, Magic: The Worlds of The Jim Henson Company’ in association with Brisbane Festival in September. Works in this exhibition are protected under the Australian Government’s Protection of Cultural Objects on Loan Act 2013. Find out more.

events.description: The Explainer Series is about exploring the questions we’re all asking.Supermarkets are part of everyday life, but there’s a lot more happening in the aisles than deciding what’s for dinner. From pricing and loyalty programs to store layouts, online shopping and the growing influence of AI, the way we buy our groceries is changing fast. The Explainer Series: Supermarkets will take a look behind the shelves to explore how Australian supermarkets became the giants they are today - and where they might be heading next. As smaller stores, home delivery, automated fulfillment and personalised shopping reshape the supermarket experience, what do we gain from all that convenience, and what might we be giving up? Join us as we unpack the power and psychology of supermarkets, the technology changing the way we shop, and what the supermarket of the future might look like.

events.title: The God of Small Things: Faith and Popular Culture
events.location: QAG, Stanley Place, South Bank
events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: 'The God of Small Things: Faith and Popular Culture' draws its title from Arundhati Roy's evocative novel to explore the omnipresence of faith in the mundane and extraordinary alike. Centred around a rare collection of embellished oleographs by Raja Ravi Varma (India, 1848-1906), the exhibition delves into the intersection between devotional imagery and popular culture, capturing the divine as a living part of everyday life. Works from the QAGOMA contemporary Asian collection complement and extend this dialogue, through the juxtaposition of religious and vernacular iconographies with contemporary reflections on belief. QAGOMA has embarked on a landmark conservation and research exchange with colleagues in India to document and conserve a rare collection of Ravi Varma works. Specialists from QAGOMA’s conservation team will collaborate with the Museum of Art and Photography (MAP), Bengaluru, to share expertise and deepen cultural ties. QAGOMA’s conservation and research exchange is supported by the Centre for Australia-India Relations. QAGOMA is proud to be a recipient of a Centre for Australia-India Relations Maitri grant.

events.title: Sorcerers from Bohemia: Picasso’s Saltimbanques
events.location: QAG, Stanley Place, South Bank
events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: 'Sorcerers from Bohemia' evokes the free-spirited world of the travelling circus performers, or saltimbanques — the subject of Pablo Picasso’s first major body of work in printmaking. 'La Suite des Saltimbanques' is a series of 15 loosely related etchings and drypoints that mark a transitional moment in the young artist’s personal and artistic development. Created on the cusp of Picasso’s Blue (1901–04) and Rose (1904–06) periods, the works are intimately connected with his paintings and drawings of the same era, including the Gallery’s own La Belle Hollandaise of 1905. On moving to Paris in 1904, 22-year-old Picasso encountered a bohemian crowd of acrobats, jugglers and street performers, whom he sketched as they rehearsed and socialised together. His early depictions focus on the vulnerability and poverty of these itinerant figures, whereas later works pay homage to their strong social bonds and the freedom of their creative lives. Appearing individually and in groups, Picasso’s saltimbanques vary widely in age and fulfil a variety of roles, from clown and friend to mother and king. Ushering in a lifelong experimentation with printmaking, 'La Suite des Saltimbanques' offers extraordinary insights into Picasso’s formative artistic concerns and the social milieu he inhabited at the time. In these sensitive and sympathetic portraits, he conveys the heft of a body, the texture of hair, a playful pose or a tender gesture with remarkable economy and elegance of line, ennobling figures who ordinarily existed on the fringes of society.

events.title: Towards a Collapsing World: German Expressionism
events.location: QAG, Stanley Place, South Bank
events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: The early decades of the twentieth century witnessed an extraordinary moment in German art, as artists responded to a modern world in flux with works that engaged deeply with contemporary society, politics and culture. ‘Towards a Collapsing World’ explores this period of significant cultural flourishing through a survey of works on paper by leading figures of German Expressionism. Rather than a single, unified approach, German Expressionism was characterised by a plurality of attitudes and styles, with artist groups such as Die Brücke (The Bridge) and Der Blaue Reiter (The Blue Rider) forming and dissolving in response to fluctuating ideologies. Common to these disparate voices was a shared belief in the power of art to effect social change. The woodcut print became an important vehicle within German Expressionism, reviving a rich medieval heritage. Its stark, simplified forms — expressed through bold, flat patterns and raw aesthetic intensity —conveyed the inner turmoil and social critique of these expressionist artists with impassioned urgency.

events.location: Vacant Assembly

The workshop will focus on natural and realistic representation of the live model in oils. Limited to 8 places. 9am - 3:30pm both days. An alla prima approach will be demonstrated, including blocking in shapes, proportion, anatomy, design, value/colour relationships, colour mixing and paint handling. events.title: Sukundimi Walks Before Me
events.location: New Farm Cinemas, 701 Brunswick St, New Farm
events.description: Q&A Panel screening. New Farm Cinemas: Mon 28 September. Q&A with Manu Peni. The Sepik River is the mother line for Papua New Guinea communities. Winding through mountains and rainforests, she is the crucial vertebrae connecting and supporting the region’s rare biodiversity and spiritual consciousness. But her livelihood and her communities are threatened by the proposal of a copper-gold mine being built near her waters, which could extract, erode and pollute an environment that she has sustained for millennia. The children of this river, led by Manu Peni, create a grassroots campaign to stop the mine from being built, resisting the forces of colonial bureaucracy and Western narratives of ‘development’ by invoking the Spirit of the river and indigenous knowledge. Sukundimi Walks Before Me explores this existential fight through lyrical expressions of existence, resistance and life along the mother river.

What happens when your life falls apart so completely that the only way forward is through the wreckage? In Holy Shigamoley, WTF Just Happened? , Deinzel Morris opens the door to the wildest, darkest, funniest, and most transformational chapter of her life. From closing a teaching business and stepping into a dangerous new world, to drugs, love, heartbreak, psychosis, hospital wards, spiritual signs, family bonds, and the long road back to herself, this memoir is a brutally honest account of what it means to break, survive, heal, and keep laughing through the chaos. Told with raw humour, deep vulnerability, and no polished filter, this is not a story about having all the answers. It is a story about losing your mind, finding your truth, and learning that even in the messiest parts of life, love can still pull you home. Messy. Dark. Funny. Honest. Human. events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: Animals have played a central part in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander culture and spiritual beliefs for over 60,000 years. Native fauna form an integral part of relationships with Country, in community and are a foundation of economies, identity and sustainability. Over many millennia of co-existence animals have been central to survival as a food source, for First Nations people they are also absorbed into lore and culture as images of totemic power; and into the ancestral creation stories that link people, land and animals. ‘Great and small’ is a celebration of these connections.

events.title: Inscribing a Life
events.location: GOMA, Stanley Place, South Bank
events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: ‘Inscribing a life’ brings artworks from across the QAGOMA Collection that register existence, histories, and time through the act of mark making. From the brute force recorded in paint on a canvas that expresses strength and vitality, to the time commitment captured in the repetition involved in making intricate forms, the desire to record and share expressions of life is championed in this exhibition. Complementing the adjacent display of ‘Archie Moore: kith and kin’ both presentations share the themes of memorials and cosmic time. Alongside artworks expressing the intensity and wonder of existence are those that celebrate and solemnly honour lives that have come to an end. These artworks speak to the importance of acknowledging loss and how through observing death the public memorial reaffirms the social fabric for the living. The importance of thinking beyond human lifespan can be seen in expressions of the cosmos, 'Inscribing a life' features artworks that grapple with the vast scale and the deep time of the universe.

events.title: Outdoor Gallery: Frazer Campbell exhibition ‘Portraiture in the Square’ at Town Square, Fish Lane Arts Precinct
events.location: Brisbane City Council What's On
events.description: ‘Portrait in the Square’ by Frazer Campbell is a pop-up exhibition presented in partnership between Brisbane City Council’s Outdoor Gallery and Fish Lane Arts Precinct. It will be on display from 5 August to 11 October 2026. Frazer Campbell’s portraiture, installed in the vitrines at Fish Lane’s Town Square, offers a contemplative pause within one of Brisbane’s busiest urban corridors. The works draw out the layered depth of individual lives in a fast-paced city environment. These original artworks act as quiet anchors, reflecting personal histories and the universal human experience and inviting passersby to recognise fragments of their own stories in another’s gaze, gesture or posture. Technically, Frazer's practice sits at the intersection of close observation and expressive mark-making, using layered surfaces and tonal nuance to suggest the complexity of identity. Frazer Campbell is a Brisbane-based emerging artist known for his intense, emotionally charged portraits in oils and acrylics. Influenced by literature, film and music, his award-winning work explores identity and connection through colour, cinematic drama, and deep empathy, all shaped by his lived experience. “I am intrigued by certain faces, especially expressions at the unhappier end of the emotional spectrum: existential angst, psychic dread.” — Frazer Campbell Frazer Campbell is featured in Council’s latest Outdoor Gallery exhibition, AMPLIFY ME! , a celebration of Brisbane artists with lived experience of disability that showcases their work in accessible outdoor spaces across the city. Grounded in inclusive arts practice, the exhibition encourages collaboration and barrier-free creativity, supporting lasting connections, inclusion and social change across Brisbane’s cultural landscape. AMPLIFY ME! is curated by Nicole Crosswell and runs from 21 November 2025 to 25 October 2026. This program is part of Council’s Outdoor Gallery, which transforms Brisbane’s laneways, streets and car parks into imaginative spaces for everyone, showcasing art in light boxes, banners, vitrines and evening projections. This program is delivered in partnership with Fish Lane Arts Precinct. Image Credit: Photography by Joseph Rucklie. Location: The vitrines at Fish Lane’s Town Square.

events.title: Beyond Henson: Puppetry and World Cinema
events.location: GOMA, Stanley Place, South Bank
events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: Inspired by the work of The Jim Henson Company and Jim Henson’s Creature Shop, the film program ‘Beyond Henson: Puppetry and World Cinema’ surveys the rich international history of storytelling through the artforms of cinema and puppetry. Presented in conjunction with the ‘Make, Believe, Magic: The Worlds of The Jim Henson Company’ exhibition (12 September 2026 – 18 April 2027), the film program delves into crafted narratives that harness traditions of puppetry and cinema to move beyond belief and into the realms of the imagination. To trace the anatomy of onscreen puppetry is to draw from millennia of performance and craft traditions that extend across the globe. From the marionette puppetry of France and the Bunraku theatre of Japan, to the Wayang Kulit puppetry of Indonesia and the British Punch and Judy show, the democratised nature of the puppet theatre has enabled an unbridled style of performance that can enact the truthful and the taboo. Taking direction from the television series Jim Henson Presents the World of Puppetry 1985, the selected titles include films that precede (and sit adjacent to) productions by The Jim Henson Company, positioning the Company’s work within the broader canon of on-screen puppetry. [sponsorLogos block] QAGOMA acknowledges the generous assistance of the National Film and Sound Archive of Australia, Canberra; the Academy Film Archive, Los Angeles; the British Film Institute, London; the NBCUniversal Archives & Collections, Los Angeles; the Library of Congress, Washington; the National Film Archive, Prague, the Australian Film Television and Radio School, Sydney and the Revival House, Perth in providing materials for this program. Program curated by Victoria Wareham, Australian Cinémathèque with additional film note writing by Rebekah Brammer.

events.title: Where the Wild Things Are Made: Jim Henson’s Creature Shop
events.location: GOMA, Stanley Place, South Bank
events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: Presented alongside the ‘Make, Believe, Magic: The Worlds of The Jim Henson Company’ special exhibition (12 September 2026 – 18 April 2027), ‘Where the Wild Things Are Made: Jim Henson’s Creature Shop’ celebrates the skill and craftsmanship of the artisans at Jim Henson’s Creature Shop. Highlighting the diverse portfolio of expressive characters and creatures made by the Company for external productions, the selected films showcase the work of Jim Henson’s Creature Shop and how it continues to shape the landscape of cinematic storytelling. An important facet of The Jim Henson Company, Jim Henson’s Creature Shop is internationally renowned for creating pioneering techniques that bring extraordinary characters and stories to life. Formally established following the release of Labyrinth in 1986, Jim Henson’s Creature Shop continues to be an enduring creative hub where performance and craftsmanship is paired with experimentation and ground-breaking technical innovation to transform the imaginary into reality. events.title: Geoffrey Burns: Ride the Chronovore
events.location: PARKER Contemporary, 38 Hope Street
events.description: Revisiting locations at different times of year, Geoffrey Burns approaches making as both a method and a measure of time. Works emerge through repeated encounters with place, where observation accumulates and memory takes form through surface and seasonal change. Ride the Chronovore considers time as an active force: consuming, transforming and leaving its evidence behind. Through repetition, Burns traces how surfaces shift, forms appear and recede, and environments register cycles that often unfold beyond human attention. Each return gathers new information while revealing what has altered, disappeared or endured. The fleeting span of a human life meets the slower tempo of the natural world, inviting an attentive and materially grounded way of looking at the quiet force of time. events.description: Step inside an exciting new residency project that invites you to experience art in unexpected ways. Artist in Residence Renee Kire takes over Museum of Brisbane’s entryway, transforming these spaces with a vibrant and dynamic mix of striking vinyl graphics and sculptural timber elements. These features create an immersive pathway that stretches across walls and ceilings, guiding you into the heart of the Museum. Drawing inspiration from Minimalism while reinterpreting the movement through a contemporary feminist lens, Kire brings fresh attention to the often-overlooked contributions of women in the field. Bright, colourful and welcoming for all visitors, the artwork is both joyful and thought-provoking. Responding directly to the architecture of the Museum, City Hall and the Brisbane cityscape, Kire’s design reveals unexpected connections between the built environment and abstract form. events.title: Fallen Angels (1995)
events.location: New Farm Cinemas, 701 Brunswick St, New Farm
events.description: Classic screening. New Farm Cinemas: Fri 25 September Lost souls reach out for human connection amidst the glimmering night world of Hong Kong in Wong Kar Wai’s hallucinatory, neon-soaked nocturne. This hyper-cool head rush plays like the dark, moody flip side to Wong’s breakout feature 'Chungking Express' as it charts the subtly interlacing fates of a handful of urban loners, including a coolly detached hitman (Leon Lai) looking to go straight, his business partner (Michelle Reis) who secretly yearns for him, and a mute delinquent (Takeshi Kaneshiro) who wreaks mischief by night. Swinging between hardboiled noir and slapstick lunacy with giddy abandon, Fallen Angels is both a dizzying, dazzling city symphony and a poignant meditation on love, loss, and longing in a metropolis that never sleeps.

events.title: 35mm The Blair Witch Project (1999)
events.location: New Farm Cinemas, 701 Brunswick St, New Farm
events.description: 35mm Film · Classic screening. REAL FILM. REAL CINEMA. At Tower Cinemas, we keep 35mm film alive. In a world of digital projection and shrinking formats, celluloid is becoming rare, and we think that matters. We hunt down original 35mm prints, often unseen for years, and put them back where they belong: on the big screen. This is cinema with depth, texture, and impact. The way it was meant to be experienced. WHY 35MM? Digital runs at 2K or 4K. 35mm? Closer to 8K. That means sharper detail, richer contrast, and deeper, more natural colour. Film simply looks and feels different—more alive. And it’s not just the format—it’s the craft. Every session is run by a real projectionist, presenting the film with care and precision. Sure, digital is consistent. Film isn’t—and that’s the point. Every print carries a history. Slight imperfections, subtle wear—that’s character. That’s warmth. That’s cinema. Three film students travel to Maryland to make a student film about a local urban legend... The Blair Witch. The three went into the woods on a two day hike to find the Blair Witch, and never came back. One year later, the students film and video were found in the woods. The footage was compiled and made into a movie. The Blair Witch Project.

events.title: Maestro 7: Symphonic Dances
events.location: Queensland Performing Arts Centre (QPAC), South Brisbane, Queensland Performing Arts Centre, Cnr Melbourne and Grey Street, South Brisbane
events.description: A celebration of music that moves the body and soul. From folk steps to final farewells, this concert is built around the joy of dance. At its heart is Rachmaninov’s final major work Symphonic Dances. Written in exile, it is filled with sweeping emotion, nostalgia, and the echoes of a life in motion. Led by Chief Conductor Umberto Clerici, it’s a powerful blend of elegance and vitality complete with an unforgettable saxophone solo. The evening begins with Dvořák’s Slavonic Dances, bursting with Bohemian spirit and irresistible folk rhythms. Then comes soloist James Crabb for the Queensland premiere of Holly Harrison’s Concerto for Classical Accordion and Orchestra, a bold, high-voltage work that dances to its own beat. Queensland Symphony Orchestra is proudly supported by Brisbane City Council.

events.title: South Brisbane Cemetery moonlight tour
events.location: South Brisbane Cemetery, Dutton Park, South Brisbane Cemetery, 185 Annerley Road, Dutton Park
events.description: Where it all began – a cemetery, a torchlight, and a thousand untold stories. Step back into the roots of Brisbane’s most beloved cemetery experiences on a Moonlight Tour , the original night-time walk that started it all. First held back circa 2009, this was the tour that lit the path – quite literally – for every Friends of South Brisbane Cemetery tour that’s followed. Unlike other tours with fixed scripts and set stops, the Moonlight Tour is delightfully unpredictable. It flows with the mood of the night and the curiosity of the group. No two nights are the same, because no two walks through history should ever be! As you meander beneath the stars and the towering trees of South Brisbane Cemetery, your guides – Tracey Olivieri and Liam Baker – will share the real stories that have shaped this extraordinary place. They’ve spent years delving into the archives, decades amongst the headstones, and countless evenings sharing their passion for the cemetery with others. You might hear about: The floods that swallowed the past The evolution of headstone art and forgotten funerary symbols The graves of the executed, tucked quietly into a shaded corner How faith divided the dead in life, and in burial The controversial “beautification” that reshaped an historical landscape A whispered ghost story (or two)…for those who like their history with a little chill And whatever questions you bring - because on this tour, you help steer the story! This is history as it should be: lived, shared, and responsive to the wonder of the moment. Whether you’re returning to where it all began or joining us for the very first time, the Moonlight Tour offers a rare and immersive way to explore South Brisbane Cemetery – not just as a resting place, but as a living archive of lives once lived. Bring your torch. Bring your curiosity. The story is still unfolding. All of our tours are not-for-profit , with all money raised going to our cemetery history and maintenance projects.

events.title: Artist in Residence: Renee Kire
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Step inside an exciting new residency project that invites you to experience art in unexpected ways. Artist in Residence Renee Kire takes over Museum of Brisbane’s entryway, transforming these spaces with a vibrant and dynamic mix of striking vinyl graphics and sculptural timber elements. These features create an immersive pathway that stretches across walls and ceilings, guiding you into the heart of the Museum. Drawing inspiration from Minimalism while reinterpreting the movement through a contemporary feminist lens, Kire brings fresh attention to the often-overlooked contributions of women in the field. Bright, colourful and welcoming for all visitors, the artwork is both joyful and thought-provoking. Responding directly to the architecture of the Museum, City Hall and the Brisbane cityscape, Kire’s design reveals unexpected connections between the built environment and abstract form. Repetition, rhythm and thoughtful details invite you to slow down, look closely and discover new perspectives. MoB’s Artist in Residence program is supported by Tim Fairfax AC. Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.title: Convict Brisbane Walking Tour
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Explore Brisbane’s colonial history on this guided tour through the city’s convict past. Beginning at the historic Windmill on Wickham Terrace and winding down to the river at Queens Wharf, the tour traces Brisbane’s transformation between 1823 and 1842 - from a remote penal outpost to an emerging free town. Hear stories of convicts and commandants, revealing how punishment, labour and authority shaped daily life. Along the way, our guides bring the settlement into focus, illuminating the social fabric and living conditions, as well as the central role of the Brisbane River in sustaining the colony. Woven throughout the tour are First Peoples’ responses to British settlement, their enduring connection to Country, and the Frontier wars that directly followed this era. Together, these intersecting stories offer a deeper understanding of how Brisbane grew from its earliest foundations into a regional centre. Tour highlights include: The Windmill, The Brisbane Crest, The Petrie Tableau, Convict-built structures and surviving remnants, Miller Park and the Commissariat Stores, Queens Wharf and, the Brisbane River. This 90‑minute, 1.75km tour is designed to suit most fitness levels, however, please note it includes walking downhill along city streets and across uneven surfaces. For more information about accessibility requirements, please refer to the Museum of Brisbane FAQs . Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.title: Maestro 7: Symphonic Dances
events.location: Queensland Performing Arts Centre (QPAC), South Brisbane, Queensland Performing Arts Centre, Cnr Melbourne and Grey Street, South Brisbane
events.description: A celebration of music that moves the body and soul. From folk steps to final farewells, this concert is built around the joy of dance. At its heart is Rachmaninov’s final major work Symphonic Dances. Written in exile, it is filled with sweeping emotion, nostalgia, and the echoes of a life in motion. Led by Chief Conductor Umberto Clerici, it’s a powerful blend of elegance and vitality complete with an unforgettable saxophone solo. The evening begins with Dvořák’s Slavonic Dances, bursting with Bohemian spirit and irresistible folk rhythms. Then comes soloist James Crabb for the Queensland premiere of Holly Harrison’s Concerto for Classical Accordion and Orchestra, a bold, high-voltage work that dances to its own beat. Queensland Symphony Orchestra is proudly supported by Brisbane City Council.

events.description: Celebrating Country and Culture through the bold designs of Magpie Goose. Museum of Brisbane is excited to collaborate with Magpie Goose, a proudly Aboriginal owned and led fashion and social enterprise, to celebrate extraordinary First Nations cultural stories and designs. This exclusive to Brisbane exhibition, developed in close collaboration with Magpie Goose owners Amanda Hayman (Wakka Wakka and Kalkadoon) and Troy Casey (Kamilaroi), offers a deep dive into the work of some of the region’s most talented First Nations artists and designers. events.title: Artist in Residence: Renee Kire
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Step inside an exciting new residency project that invites you to experience art in unexpected ways. Artist in Residence Renee Kire takes over Museum of Brisbane’s entryway, transforming these spaces with a vibrant and dynamic mix of striking vinyl graphics and sculptural timber elements. These features create an immersive pathway that stretches across walls and ceilings, guiding you into the heart of the Museum. Drawing inspiration from Minimalism while reinterpreting the movement through a contemporary feminist lens, Kire brings fresh attention to the often-overlooked contributions of women in the field. Bright, colourful and welcoming for all visitors, the artwork is both joyful and thought-provoking. Responding directly to the architecture of the Museum, City Hall and the Brisbane cityscape, Kire’s design reveals unexpected connections between the built environment and abstract form. Repetition, rhythm and thoughtful details invite you to slow down, look closely and discover new perspectives. MoB’s Artist in Residence program is supported by Tim Fairfax AC. Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.title: Warrajamba
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Follow the mermaid in the bay. Dive into story, culture and hands-on creativity with our latest Artist in Residence, Quandamooka artist Delvene Cockatoo-Collins. Journey alongside Delvene to the shores of Minjerribah and discover the ancestral story of Warrajamba, the mermaid, a living cultural legacy that Delvene continues to explore as she searches for its lost ending. Get hands-on and create your own mermaid or dugong using artist-designed stamps, connecting with the stories of Warrajamba and Yungong, the dugong. Discover Delvene’s powerful sculptural work made from materials gathered from Country - yungair/yungaire (freshwater reed), talwalpin (beach hibiscus cotton tree), and quampie shell. Come and be immersed in a space that celebrates care for land, sea and story. MoB’s Artist in Residence program is supported by Tim Fairfax AC. The Creative Space is proudly supported by Major Partner Brisbane Airport and generously supported by Ian and Cass George, and Holly and John Livingstone. Warrajamba is supported by the Queensland Government through Arts Queensland. Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.title: Botanic By Night: NightGlow
events.location: Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha, Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha, 152 Mt Coot-tha Road, Toowong
events.description: Botanic By Night: NightGlow makes its Brisbane debut at Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha from 25 September to 10 October, transforming the Gardens into a magical after-dark outdoor art experience. Visitors will journey along an enchanting 800-metre route featuring 11 larger-than-life illuminated animal sculptures inspired by Queensland's native wildlife. Designed by Ample Projects in collaboration with First Nations artists Casey Coolwell-Fisher and Nathan Peckham, Botanic By Night: NightGlow combines art, storytelling and sound to celebrate the animals, habitats and stories that shape Queensland's natural environment. From kangaroos and koalas to platypus, dingoes and green tree frogs, each artwork offers a unique encounter, inviting visitors to wander, explore and connect with nature in a whole new way. Perfect for families, friends and date nights, Botanic By Night: NightGlow also features a dedicated food truck precinct.

events.location: New Farm Cinemas, 701 Brunswick St, New Farm
events.description: Festival screening. New Farm Cinemas. After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Anderson, The X-Files), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

events.title: Fallen Angels (1995)
events.location: New Farm Cinemas, 701 Brunswick St, New Farm
events.description: Classic screening. New Farm Cinemas: Fri 25 September Lost souls reach out for human connection amidst the glimmering night world of Hong Kong in Wong Kar Wai’s hallucinatory, neon-soaked nocturne. This hyper-cool head rush plays like the dark, moody flip side to Wong’s breakout feature 'Chungking Express' as it charts the subtly interlacing fates of a handful of urban loners, including a coolly detached hitman (Leon Lai) looking to go straight, his business partner (Michelle Reis) who secretly yearns for him, and a mute delinquent (Takeshi Kaneshiro) who wreaks mischief by night. Swinging between hardboiled noir and slapstick lunacy with giddy abandon, Fallen Angels is both a dizzying, dazzling city symphony and a poignant meditation on love, loss, and longing in a metropolis that never sleeps.

events.title: English linked sword dance
events.location: Moorooka Community Centre, Moorooka, Moorooka Community Centre, 40 Gainsborough Street, Moorooka
events.description: Step into the rhythm of steel and tradition with English Linked Sword Dance. This striking folk dance brings together precision, teamwork, and centuries of English heritage. Dancers move in tight formations, each holding a sword linked to the next, creating intricate patterns, locks, and woven figures that flow seamlessly with the music. The highlight comes when the swords are joined to form a star or “lock,” lifted high in a dramatic display of skill and unity. Energetic, powerful, and deeply communal, English linked sword dance is as much about cooperation as it is about spectacle. No solo stars here - every movement depends on trust, timing, and connection with the whole team. Whether you’re drawn by history, live music, or the thrill of learning something bold and different, this is your chance to be part of a living tradition. Join us, take a sword, and become one of the links.

events.location: New Farm Cinemas, 701 Brunswick St, New Farm
events.description: Classic screening. New Farm Cinemas: Fri 25 September Lost souls reach out for human connection amidst the glimmering night world of Hong Kong in Wong Kar Wai’s hallucinatory, neon-soaked nocturne. This hyper-cool head rush plays like the dark, moody flip side to Wong’s breakout feature 'Chungking Express' as it charts the subtly interlacing fates of a handful of urban loners, including a coolly detached hitman (Leon Lai) looking to go straight, his business partner (Michelle Reis) who secretly yearns for him, and a mute delinquent (Takeshi Kaneshiro) who wreaks mischief by night. Swinging between hardboiled noir and slapstick lunacy with giddy abandon, Fallen Angels is both a dizzying, dazzling city symphony and a poignant meditation on love, loss, and longing in a metropolis that never sleeps.

events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Celebrating Country and Culture through the bold designs of Magpie Goose. Museum of Brisbane is excited to collaborate with Magpie Goose, a proudly Aboriginal owned and led fashion and social enterprise, to celebrate extraordinary First Nations cultural stories and designs. This exclusive to Brisbane exhibition, developed in close collaboration with Magpie Goose owners Amanda Hayman (Wakka Wakka and Kalkadoon) and Troy Casey (Kamilaroi), offers a deep dive into the work of some of the region’s most talented First Nations artists and designers. Using clothing as a canvas for storytelling, this exciting collaboration will connect audiences with the rich and diverse cultural expressions of First Nations communities in Queensland and beyond. Discover the artists and stories behind the brand that’s making a difference, one garment at a time. Stories You Wear: Magpie Goose is supported by the Queensland Government through Arts Queensland. Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture. For more information, visit MoB website. Image: Magpie Goose x Quandamooka Artists, by Amanda Hayman & Troy Casey, Country to Couture, 2025, Photo by Dylan Buckee.

events.title: Artist in Residence: Renee Kire
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Step inside an exciting new residency project that invites you to experience art in unexpected ways. Artist in Residence Renee Kire takes over Museum of Brisbane’s entryway, transforming these spaces with a vibrant and dynamic mix of striking vinyl graphics and sculptural timber elements. These features create an immersive pathway that stretches across walls and ceilings, guiding you into the heart of the Museum. Drawing inspiration from Minimalism while reinterpreting the movement through a contemporary feminist lens, Kire brings fresh attention to the often-overlooked contributions of women in the field. Bright, colourful and welcoming for all visitors, the artwork is both joyful and thought-provoking. Responding directly to the architecture of the Museum, City Hall and the Brisbane cityscape, Kire’s design reveals unexpected connections between the built environment and abstract form. Repetition, rhythm and thoughtful details invite you to slow down, look closely and discover new perspectives. MoB’s Artist in Residence program is supported by Tim Fairfax AC. Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.title: Warrajamba
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Follow the mermaid in the bay. Dive into story, culture and hands-on creativity with our latest Artist in Residence, Quandamooka artist Delvene Cockatoo-Collins. Journey alongside Delvene to the shores of Minjerribah and discover the ancestral story of Warrajamba, the mermaid, a living cultural legacy that Delvene continues to explore as she searches for its lost ending. Get hands-on and create your own mermaid or dugong using artist-designed stamps, connecting with the stories of Warrajamba and Yungong, the dugong. Discover Delvene’s powerful sculptural work made from materials gathered from Country - yungair/yungaire (freshwater reed), talwalpin (beach hibiscus cotton tree), and quampie shell. Come and be immersed in a space that celebrates care for land, sea and story. MoB’s Artist in Residence program is supported by Tim Fairfax AC. The Creative Space is proudly supported by Major Partner Brisbane Airport and generously supported by Ian and Cass George, and Holly and John Livingstone. Warrajamba is supported by the Queensland Government through Arts Queensland. Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.title: Gathering: Muralappi Arts: Jessica Skeen
events.location: Queen Street Mall, Brisbane City, Queen Street Mall, Queen Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Gathering presents Muralappi Arts: Jessica Skeen. Jessica Skeen is a contemporary Aboriginal artist and founder of Muralappi Arts, an Indigenous family-owned business with a proud legacy spanning four generations. A Biri and Kuku Thaypan woman from North Queensland, Jessica was raised in Logan and continues to live and work there today. Her artistic practice is grounded in culture, storytelling, and connection to Country, with works that explore themes of healing, identity, and community. Through murals, canvas artworks, and functional art pieces, Jessica creates powerful visual narratives that foster reflection, understanding, and connection. Her work has been featured in hospitals, public spaces, and community initiatives throughout Queensland, enriching shared spaces with stories that celebrate Aboriginal culture and lived experience. Dedicated to sharing culture and knowledge, Jessica also delivers engaging, hands-on workshops that inspire creativity while promoting cultural understanding and respect. Join us on Wednesday 30 September, from 12 noon to 1pm, at the Queen Street Mall Main Stage for a special Muralappi Arts display and showcase presented by Jessica Skeen. This Gathering event is produced by Cre8tive Nations.

events.description: Botanic By Night: NightGlow makes its Brisbane debut at Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha from 25 September to 10 October, transforming the Gardens into a magical after-dark outdoor art experience. Visitors will journey along an enchanting 800-metre route featuring 11 larger-than-life illuminated animal sculptures inspired by Queensland's native wildlife. Designed by Ample Projects in collaboration with First Nations artists Casey Coolwell-Fisher and Nathan Peckham, Botanic By Night: NightGlow combines art, storytelling and sound to celebrate the animals, habitats and stories that shape Queensland's natural environment. From kangaroos and koalas to platypus, dingoes and green tree frogs, each artwork offers a unique encounter, inviting visitors to wander, explore and connect with nature in a whole new way. Perfect for families, friends and date nights, Botanic By Night: NightGlow also features a dedicated food truck precinct.

events.title: Ancient Channels- Static Spirit Album Launch

events.description: Ancient Channels is a Brisbane post-punk outfit known for its swirling guitar landscapes, dream-pop sensibilities, and a cinematic approach to songwriting. The project channels a love of ’80s post punk, modern psych-pop, and atmospheric post-punk into a sound that feels expansive yet intimate. Formed against the backdrop of Brisbane’s tightly knit independent music community, Ancient Channels quickly stood out for their ability to fuse shimmering textures with grounded, emotionally honest lyricism. Their songs unfold like scenes with rich layers of reverb, swirling effects, and melodic guitar interplay creating a sonic world that invites listeners in rather than overwhelms.The result is music that feels both nostalgic and exploratory: echoes of The Cure and Siouxsie And The Banshees woven into something distinctly their own. Onstage, Ancient Channels delivers immersive performances marked by dynamic energy and detailed soundscapes. The band’s live sets move fluidly from atmospheric introspection to powerful crescendos, showcasing a versatility that resonates with audiences across Brisbane’s venues and festivals. With each release, Ancient Channels continues to refine and expand their sonic palette, building a reputation as one of Brisbane’s most compelling underground acts. Their work captures the restless creativity of the city’s scene while carving out a unique identity that is textured and heartfelt. events.title: Artist in Residence: Renee Kire
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Step inside an exciting new residency project that invites you to experience art in unexpected ways. Artist in Residence Renee Kire takes over Museum of Brisbane’s entryway, transforming these spaces with a vibrant and dynamic mix of striking vinyl graphics and sculptural timber elements. These features create an immersive pathway that stretches across walls and ceilings, guiding you into the heart of the Museum. Drawing inspiration from Minimalism while reinterpreting the movement through a contemporary feminist lens, Kire brings fresh attention to the often-overlooked contributions of women in the field. Bright, colourful and welcoming for all visitors, the artwork is both joyful and thought-provoking. Responding directly to the architecture of the Museum, City Hall and the Brisbane cityscape, Kire’s design reveals unexpected connections between the built environment and abstract form. Repetition, rhythm and thoughtful details invite you to slow down, look closely and discover new perspectives. MoB’s Artist in Residence program is supported by Tim Fairfax AC. Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.title: Justene Williams: Once We Were Mudskippers
events.location: QAG, Stanley Place, South Bank
events.source: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA)
events.description: Spanning performative videos, sculpture, sound and installation from the past 20 years, including a wealth of new works, ‘Once We Were Mudskippers’ emphasises the aesthetic ambition of Justene Williams’s expansive practice. Like the amphibious fish invoked by the exhibition’s title, which exist between worlds, Williams’s artworks are an amalgam of materials and approaches and remain grounded in art history while reflecting contemporary issues. Adopting a do-it-yourself strategy, Williams fuses disparate textures and concepts into compelling artworks that speak to her belief that our shared future can be forged with resources at hand and transformed by the imagination. Williams’s artworks address ideals of beauty, careerist and consumerist pressures, the strangeness of living in both the physical body and virtual space, and human connections to rituals and the afterlife. ‘Once We Were Mudskippers’ is characterised by Justene Williams’s unwavering conviction that art is a world where artists and audiences can experiment and commune.

events.title: Dry Leaf
events.location: New Farm Cinemas, 701 Brunswick St, New Farm
events.description: Premiere screening. New Farm Cinemas: Sat 3 October. Presented in partnership with Container: Brisbane Film Society and the Institute of Modern Art (IMA). A Plainwater Films release. QLD PREMIERE. When sports photographer Lisa vanished, she was working on an assignment documenting ramshackle football fields across the country. She has left behind a letter for her parents in Tbilisi instructing them not to follow her – a request that her father, Irakli (played by the filmmaker’s own father, David Koberidze), disregards. He attempts to retrace her cross-country path together with her colleague Levan – who, like many of the characters in this gentle and transfixing saga, happens to be invisible – but theirs is destined to be a sublimely digressive quest, punctuated by curious encounters. Shot entirely on an old Sony Ericsson camera phone and unfolding across an epic timescale, Alexandre Koberidze’s latest feature – winner of both a Competition Special Mention and the FIPRESCI Prize at Locarno Film Festival – combines the sense of melancholic whimsy that distinguished his previous feature, 'What Do We See When We Look at the Sky?', with its daring formal gambit, giving its images of the Georgian countryside a surprising, pixelated beauty at times verging on abstraction.

events.title: Artist in Residence: Renee Kire

events.description: Step inside an exciting new residency project that invites you to experience art in unexpected ways. Artist in Residence Renee Kire takes over Museum of Brisbane’s entryway, transforming these spaces with a vibrant and dynamic mix of striking vinyl graphics and sculptural timber elements. These features create an immersive pathway that stretches across walls and ceilings, guiding you into the heart of the Museum. Drawing inspiration from Minimalism while reinterpreting the movement through a contemporary feminist lens, Kire brings fresh attention to the often-overlooked contributions of women in the field. Bright, colourful and welcoming for all visitors, the artwork is both joyful and thought-provoking. Responding directly to the architecture of the Museum, City Hall and the Brisbane cityscape, Kire’s design reveals unexpected connections between the built environment and abstract form. Repetition, rhythm and thoughtful details invite you to slow down, look closely and discover new perspectives. MoB’s Artist in Residence program is supported by Tim Fairfax AC. Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.description: Follow the mermaid in the bay. Dive into story, culture and hands-on creativity with our latest Artist in Residence, Quandamooka artist Delvene Cockatoo-Collins. Journey alongside Delvene to the shores of Minjerribah and discover the ancestral story of Warrajamba, the mermaid, a living cultural legacy that Delvene continues to explore as she searches for its lost ending. Get hands-on and create your own mermaid or dugong using artist-designed stamps, connecting with the stories of Warrajamba and Yungong, the dugong. Discover Delvene’s powerful sculptural work made from materials gathered from Country - yungair/yungaire (freshwater reed), talwalpin (beach hibiscus cotton tree), and quampie shell. Come and be immersed in a space that celebrates care for land, sea and story. MoB’s Artist in Residence program is supported by Tim Fairfax AC. From kangaroos and koalas to platypus, dingoes and green tree frogs, each artwork offers a unique encounter, inviting visitors to wander, explore and connect with nature in a whole new way. This exhibition represents a small sample of our teams’ favourite finds – the weird and whimsical, the cute and curious. We gratefully acknowledge the hundreds of donors who generously supported the QAGOMA Foundation’s ‘Unlock the Collection’ campaign to digitise the Collection and make artworks more accessible and discoverable online including this diverse range of artworks, from small figures to small frogs. These are some of the artworks we have recently prepared for photography, and just some of the works which made us smile.

events.title: Capturing Beauty – Solo show by Carol Oh
events.location: Petrie Terrace Gallery, 3/162 Petrie Terrace
events.description: [vc_row css=”.vc_custom_1523319263370{padding-top: 20px !important;padding-bottom: 30px !important;}”][vc_column][vc_separator color=”custom” border_width=”10″ accent_color=”#4ba686″][vc_column_text]Brisbane-based artist Carol Oh creates works in oil paint and pen that celebrate the timeless beauty of the human form, nature, architecture, and the quiet poetry of everyday life. Her diverse body of work encompasses exquisite floral studies, portraiture, figurative subjects, landscapes, and finely detailed pen drawings of Rome and its enduring architectural splendour. Drawing and painting from a young age, Carol has cultivated a lifelong passion for capturing beauty, atmosphere, and character. Her work reflects a deep appreciation for both the grandeur and subtlety found in the world around us. This exhibition, Capturing Beauty, brings together a collection of portraiture, figurative, floral, and landscape works. Through her art, Carol invites viewers into moments of reflection and connection, creating evocative imagery that lingers in the memory and resonates beyond the canvas. She continues to expand her artistic practice and welcomes commissioned work. Exhibition will be on show at RQAS Brisbane Gallery from Wednesday, 23rd of September to Sunday, 27th of September.[/vc_column_text][vc_separator color=”custom” border_width=”10″ accent_color=”#4ba686″][vc_single_image image=”26108″ img_size=”full”][/vc_column][/vc_row]

events.description: Discover the fascinating world of flowers and the peculiar Pollinators who work with them at our Spring hub school holiday activities at the Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha. Get your hands dirty and turn science into art by making 3D clay pollen models and sensational seed balls. Finally compile all your field notes and decorate them with pen or a paintbrush while you discover more about the precious pollinators who help to keep our flowers fantastic and our fruit plentiful. Bring a picnic blanket and lunch to enjoy on our grassy lawn. Note: Children under 16 are to be accompanied by an adult. Location : Meet at the Auditorium lawn. Please wear a hat and enclosed shoes; and bring a keep cup or water bottle. This workshop supports the Botanic Gardens' commitment to creating a plant loving community dedicated to putting the plant back into planet. For more information, send an email .

} } ⚖️ Watch drama | 🗳️ Cast a vote | 🕵️ Crack the case ⭐ You've been called for jury duty. Step into a thrilling courtroom drama where the audience is the jury. Listen to testimonies, analyze evidence, and ultimately decide… guilty or not guilty? It's not theatre you watch. It's justice you deliver. The Million Dollar Murder Inspired by true events, this gripping courtroom drama pulls you into a world where greed, passion, and revenge collide — and where the line between victim and villain is razor-thin. The accused stands in the dock, but is this a cold-blooded killer, or a pawn in a far more dangerous game? No DNA evidence. A tangled web of desire and betrayal. And a divorce worth millions. Every witness has a reason to lie. Every motive points somewhere different. Can you untangle the truth before the verdict is cast? 🚩 This experience includes themes of murder and violent death, domestic violence, emotional manipulation. There is a detailed discussion of a homicide. The performance contains moments of intense emotional conflict. Highlights 🤩 Enjoy a live theatre courtroom drama where you decide the final verdict 🫵 Vote during key moments - your decisions shape hidden angles in the case, making every show different! 🕵️‍♂️ Dissect witness testimonies, unpack evidence, and weigh every argument 🎢 A high-stakes case full of twists - more turns than a rollercoaster, and a verdict only you can deliver How it works 1 Take your seat Arrive 30 min early. Doors close at show time — late entry is not permitted. 2 Hear the case Track every testimony, spot the contradictions, and vote at key moments to steer the trial. 3 Deliver your verdict The jury speaks. Guilty or not guilty - the outcome rests entirely with you. Practical info ⏳ Duration 60 minutes Doors open 30 min before 📍 Venue Old Museum Brisbane 480 Gregory Terrace, Bowen Hills, QLD 4006, Australia 👤 Age 12+ Under 16s must be with an adult ♿ Accessibility Wheelchair accessible Wheelchair zone available ✨ Groups & Private Take the stand 30+ people or private show 🎁 Gift card Send gift Gift memories to someone special Frequently asked questions About the experience What is The Jury Experience and what can I expect? The Jury Experience is an immersive courtroom drama where you become part of the story as a juror. Analyze testimonies, cross-examinations, and evidence to uncover the truth - your vote determines the accused's fate. How long does the experience last? The experience lasts approximately 1 hour. Will there be strobe lights? No, there will not be any strobe lights. Are seats numbered? No, seats are not assigned. Seating is first-come, first-served within the zone you select when purchasing your ticket. About your tickets What are the different types of tickets available? A reserve: Best visibility B reserve: Good visibility, located on the sides C reserve: Fair visibility, positioned further back D reserve: Fair visibility, positioned further back behind C reserve Can I buy a ticket on site on the day of the event? Tickets cannot be purchased on site. All tickets must be purchased via the app or website (feverup.com) before arriving at the event. Is it necessary to buy a ticket for my carer? Guests requiring assistance are entitled to one free pass for their personal assistant/support worker. Contact us to receive a voucher for a free carer ticket (based on availability). The regular ticket must be shown together with the carer ticket at entry. Can I change the date of my ticket? Are refunds allowed? Subject to availability, date/time changes are permitted up to 48 hours before the start time. Tickets are non-refundable except as required under Australian Consumer Law. Can I transfer my tickets to another person? Yes, tickets can be transferred to any other Fever account at no additional cost via "Transfer tickets" in the Fever app. Where can I find my ticket? Do I need to print it out? Your ticket is in the "Tickets" section of the Fever app, and also in your purchase confirmation email. You do not need to print it - it's validated via the app on arrival. Access & venue Where does the show take place? The show takes place at The Old Museum, 480 Gregory Terrace, Bowen Hills QLD 4006, Australia. Does the experience take place indoors or outdoors? This experience takes place indoors in a heated/air-conditioned venue. Are food and drinks available on site for purchase? No, food and drinks are not available for purchase on site. Are animals allowed? Animals, except assistance animals, are not allowed. Is the venue accessible? Yes, the event is held in an accessible venue. Accessible seating is limited to Zone A and B only. Are there chairs available? Can I be seated during the experience? Yes, this is a seated experience - seating is available for every guest. Will toilet facilities be available on site? Yes, the venue has toilets; on-site staff can direct you. Is there parking on site? There is no dedicated venue parking, but surrounding parking garages and limited street parking are available. Public transport or sustainable alternatives are recommended. Is cloakroom service available? Unfortunately, this location does not have a cloakroom service. Can I take photos or use my phone during the performance? Photos and videos can only be taken during the curtain call, without flash. Phones must be in silent mode throughout the performance. Can I leave during the performance? What items are prohibited? Out of respect for the performers and the audience, you may not leave your seat except in an emergency. Prohibited items include smoking/vaping, external alcohol, hot food or drinks, strong-smelling food or glass, audio recording devices, drugs, flammables, torches, lasers, professional cameras, promotional items, and selfie sticks/tripods. events.title: School holiday activity - Spring hub - Flower power
events.location: Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha, Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha, 152 Mt Coot-tha Road, Toowong
events.description: Discover the fascinating world of flowers and the peculiar Pollinators who work with them at our Spring hub school holiday activities at the Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha. Take off on a scientific exploration of our Sensory Garden, bursting with blooms of all shapes and sizes and bring your findings back to the hub where you can take a closer look with microscopes and magnifying glasses. Get your hands dirty and turn science into art by making 3D clay pollen models and sensational seed balls. Finally compile all your field notes and decorate them with pen or a paintbrush while you discover more about the precious pollinators who help to keep our flowers fantastic and our fruit plentiful. Bring a picnic blanket and lunch to enjoy on our grassy lawn. Note: Children under 16 are to be accompanied by an adult. Location : Meet at the Auditorium lawn. Please wear a hat and enclosed shoes; and bring a keep cup or water bottle. This workshop supports the Botanic Gardens' commitment to creating a plant loving community dedicated to putting the plant back into planet. For more information, send an email .

events.title: Meet Wildlife Neighbours (6+ years)
events.location: Karawatha Forest Park and Discovery Centre, Karawatha Forest Park and Discovery Centre, 149 Acacia Road, Karawatha
events.description: Get up close and discover the feathered, furry and scaly friends that live in our neighbourhoods. Brisbane is Australia’s most biodiverse capital city. Native wildlife live all around us — from our backyards to local parks and nature reserves. But have you ever met these unique animals face to face? Join our wildlife expert for an engaging and immersive session in nature, where you'll meet your wild neighbours and some of Brisbane's most iconic animals. Discover what makes them special, how they live, and the vital role they play in our ecosystems. Your actions matter. By learning more about our native species, you’ll be empowered to make simple changes — like planting native vegetation or keeping pets indoors at night. These actions help protect our incredible biodiversity and ensure our wildlife neighbours continue to thrive. Requirements on the day: Arrive minimum 10 minutes early to check in with staff at the centre. All children must be accompanied and directly supervised by an adult. Wear a hat, sun-safe clothing, fully enclosed shoes, sunscreen, and bring insect repellent as some shows may take place outside. Bring water and a snack if required, as there are no food outlets on site. Note: Events are subject to weather and environmental conditions and may be cancelled on the day.

events.description: Brisbane is Australia’s most biodiverse capital city. Native wildlife live all around us — from our backyards to local parks and nature reserves. events.title: Convict Brisbane Walking Tour
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Explore Brisbane’s colonial history on this guided tour through the city’s convict past. Beginning at the historic Windmill on Wickham Terrace and winding down to the river at Queens Wharf, the tour traces Brisbane’s transformation between 1823 and 1842 - from a remote penal outpost to an emerging free town. Hear stories of convicts and commandants, revealing how punishment, labour and authority shaped daily life. Along the way, our guides bring the settlement into focus, illuminating the social fabric and living conditions, as well as the central role of the Brisbane River in sustaining the colony. Woven throughout the tour are First Peoples’ responses to British settlement, their enduring connection to Country, and the Frontier wars that directly followed this era. Together, these intersecting stories offer a deeper understanding of how Brisbane grew from its earliest foundations into a regional centre. Tour highlights include: The Windmill, The Brisbane Crest, The Petrie Tableau, Convict-built structures and surviving remnants, Miller Park and the Commissariat Stores, Queens Wharf and, the Brisbane River. This 90‑minute, 1.75km tour is designed to suit most fitness levels, however, please note it includes walking downhill along city streets and across uneven surfaces. For more information about accessibility requirements, please refer to the Museum of Brisbane FAQs . Museum of Brisbane is Brisbane City Council’s leading history and art museum where you can experience our city’s vibrant culture.

events.title: Brisbane's True Crime Tour
events.location: Brisbane City Hall
events.description: Highlights 🌃 Peel back the glamour of modern Brisbane to reveal a brutal and bloody history 🕵️‍♂️ Retrace the steps of the city’s most infamous brawlers, fraudsters, and outlaws 🚶‍♂️ Explore historic buildings and hidden alleyways where dark secrets still linger 😱 Hear jaw-dropping true stories of love triangles gone wrong and lawless underworlds General Info 📅 Date & Time: choose date and time directly in ticket selector 📍 Location: Meets at the front entrance of the Brisbane City Hall in King George Square 👤 Age: Recommended for mature audiences ⏳ Duration: approx. 1.5 hours ❓ Weather Policy: Tours run in most conditions. Dark Stories will contact you via SMS/Email at least 90 minutes before start time if weather impacts the tour. Description Don’t let the bright lights of "Bris-Vegas" fool you. Beneath the bustling city streets lies a dark past that the city tried to forget. Join us for a leisurely guided walking tour that transports you back to a seemingly lawless world of crime and intrigue. From notorious historical figures to the criminal underbelly that once plagued the city, this investigation uncovers the secrets hiding behind every historic facade. Forget what you think you know about Brisbane and prepare for a trip down a memory lane you never knew existed. Get your tickets for Brisbane’s True Crime Tour and take a walk on the dark side!

events.title: Meet Wildlife Neighbours (6+ years)
events.location: Boondall Wetlands Environment Centre, Boondall Wetlands Environment Centre, 31 Paperbark Drive (entry via Stanworth Rd), Boondall
events.description: Get up close and discover the feathered, furry and scaly friends that live in our neighbourhoods. Brisbane is Australia’s most biodiverse capital city. Native wildlife live all around us — from our backyards to local parks and nature reserves. But have you ever met these unique animals face to face? Join our wildlife expert for an engaging and immersive session in nature, where you'll meet your wild neighbours and some of Brisbane's most iconic animals. Discover what makes them special, how they live, and the vital role they play in our ecosystems. Your actions matter. By learning more about our native species, you’ll be empowered to make simple changes — like planting native vegetation or keeping pets indoors at night. These actions help protect our incredible biodiversity and ensure our wildlife neighbours continue to thrive. Requirements on the day: Arrive minimum 10 minutes early to check in with staff at the centre. All children must be accompanied and directly supervised by an adult. Wear a hat, sun-safe clothing, fully enclosed shoes, sunscreen, and bring insect repellent as some shows may take place outside. Bring water and a snack if required, as there are no food outlets on site. Note: Events are subject to weather and environmental conditions and may be cancelled on the day.

events.title: Create a poppy suncatcher
events.location: Anzac Square, Brisbane City, Anzac Square, 228 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Pop into Anzac Square Memorial Galleries during the spring school holidays to create your own poppy suncatcher. Let's get crafty! Suitable for all ages, this free family-friendly craft activity is available between 10 am – 4pm daily from 20 September to 4 October (closed Saturdays). Bookings are not required, simply visit the craft table in our Post World War II Gallery. Facilitated by our knowledgeable team, this activity will explore the special connection between poppies and Australia’s military past. A resilient flower, the red poppy was amongst the first to return to bloom in the fields of France and Belgium after World War I, emerging as a symbol of remembrance for the Allied soldiers who fell in battle. Once you've created your poppy suncatcher, stay to explore the Memorial Galleries, embarking on an interactive journey from World War I to today, before taking time to reflect on the remarkable stories of bravery and sacrifice in the tranquil parklands.

After a seven-year hiatus following the devastating loss of their beloved bandmate Chester Bennington, LINKIN PARK’S remaining members struggle to find their way forward. Their shared history and enduring friendship, combined with the fresh perspective of two new band members spark a renewed creative energy that leads them on a transformative journey of artistic reinvention. events.title: Clock Tower Tour

events.description: Discover the hidden secrets of your heritage-listed City Hall building with a guided tour of Brisbane’s iconic Clock Tower. The Clock Tower Tour is a “must do” while in Brisbane! For many years, City Hall’s Clock Tower elevated the building to Brisbane’s tallest, offering visitors a magnificent 360 degree view of the city around them. Whilst the view has changed significantly over the last 90 years, the time-honoured tradition of “taking a trip up the tower” happily continues at Museum of Brisbane. The Clock Tower Tour includes a ride in one of Brisbane’s oldest working cage lifts, a look behind Australia’s largest analogue clock faces and time to explore the observation platform that shares a unique perspective of your city. See if you can catch a glimpse of the bells! Make a booking online today to secure your spot! Spaces are limited and fill up quickly. events.title: Tejaswini Bhava Abhiyan
events.location: Northgate Hall, Northgate, Northgate Hall, 34 Ridge Street, Northgate
events.description: Tejaswini Bhava Abhiyan — A girls and women only event. Tejaswini Abhiyaan is a community initiative organised by Shri Yog Vedant Seva Samiti, in association with the Mahila Utthan Mandal wing of Sant Shri Asharam Ji Ashram, with the aim of empowering girls and young women by nurturing confidence, positive thinking, inner strength, self-belief, and a strong sense of purpose. The word Tejaswini describes a girl who embodies tejas (inner radiance), confidence, positivity, courage, self-esteem and inner strength. The initiative is founded on the belief that every girl possesses unique strengths, abilities and potential that can be nurtured and developed. Just as a small seed contains the potential to grow into a magnificent tree, every individual has the potential for growth and excellence. In the same way, every girl has a Tejaswini within her. Tejaswini Abhiyaan seeks to encourage girls to recognise their strengths, discover their potential and develop the confidence to make a positive contribution to their families, communities and society. Through educational, cultural, creative and community activities, the initiative promotes positive values, confidence, leadership, self-awareness, personal development and an appreciation of Indian cultural heritage, traditions and values. The initiative provides an encouraging environment where girls can learn, participate, express themselves, develop their abilities and build confidence while connecting with cultural traditions and the wider community. The vision of Tejaswini Abhiyaan is simple: to inspire every girl to discover, nurture and awaken the Tejaswini within her.

events.title: Clock Tower Tour
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Discover the hidden secrets of your heritage-listed City Hall building with a guided tour of Brisbane’s iconic Clock Tower. The Clock Tower Tour is a “must do” while in Brisbane! Whilst the view has changed significantly over the last 90 years, the time-honoured tradition of “taking a trip up the tower” happily continues at Museum of Brisbane. events.title: Create a poppy suncatcher
events.location: Anzac Square, Brisbane City, Anzac Square, 228 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Pop into Anzac Square Memorial Galleries during the spring school holidays to create your own poppy suncatcher. Let's get crafty! Suitable for all ages, this free family-friendly craft activity is available between 10am–4pm daily from 20 September to 4 October (closed Saturdays). Bookings are not required, simply visit the craft table in our Post World War II Gallery. Facilitated by our knowledgeable team, this activity will explore the special connection between poppies and Australia’s military past. A resilient flower, the red poppy was amongst the first to return to bloom in the fields of France and Belgium after World War I, emerging as a symbol of remembrance for the Allied soldiers who fell in battle. Once you've created your poppy suncatcher, stay to explore the Memorial Galleries, embarking on an interactive journey from World War I to today, before taking time to reflect on the remarkable stories of bravery and sacrifice in the tranquil parklands.

events.title: Clock Tower Tour
events.location: Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City, Museum of Brisbane, Brisbane City Hall, 64 Adelaide Street, Brisbane City
events.description: Discover the hidden secrets of your heritage-listed City Hall building with a guided tour of Brisbane’s iconic Clock Tower. The Clock Tower Tour is a “must do” while in Brisbane! For many years, City Hall’s Clock Tower elevated the building to Brisbane’s tallest, offering visitors a magnificent 360 degree view of the city around them. Whilst the view has changed significantly over the last 90 years, the time-honoured tradition of “taking a trip up the tower” happily continues at Museum of Brisbane. The Clock Tower Tour includes a ride in one of Brisbane’s oldest working cage lifts, a look behind Australia’s largest analogue clock faces and time to explore the observation platform that shares a unique perspective of your city. See if you can catch a glimpse of the bells! Make a booking online today to secure your spot! Spaces are limited and fill up quickly. events.location: Fever Skygate | Exhibition and Immersive Experience centre, 30-34 The Circuit, Skygate Home and Life Centre, Brisbane Airport
